The level flag is not a reason, but 'too' is correct English here: 'The soup wasn't too hot to eat' (= you could eat it) is fine, so a wrong option fits. A result clause now rules it out. Options stay from the card ('Degree: very, really, quite, extremely, too + adjective ... enough comes after the adjective').

fix.q: Choose the correct option: The soup wasn't hot ___ to eat, so I heated it up again.
fix.why: *enough* comes after the adjective: *The soup wasn't hot enough to eat, so I heated it up again.* *too, very, quite* go before the adjective, and *wasn't too hot to eat* would mean it was fine to eat, so you would not heat it again.
fix.why_lv: *enough* ir aiz īpašības vārda: *The soup wasn't hot enough to eat, so I heated it up again.* *too, very, quite* ir pirms īpašības vārda, un *wasn't too hot to eat* nozīmētu, ka zupu varēja ēst, tāpēc to nesildītu vēlreiz.
